observations: Photo 0 shows a Nikon AF-S NIKKOR lens with visible text “AF-S NIKKOR” and “50mm 1/8G” (appears to be “50mm 1.8G”).
Photo 1 shows the front element and the side label area; the lens front ring reads “Nikon” and “AF-S NIKKOR”, and “50mm 1.8G” is visible on the barrel.
Photo 2 shows the rear/side of the lens with “Nikon” and “AF-S NIKKOR” markings; the rear glass looks clear but there is no close-up of coating/edges.

claims.evidence: No photo evidence of country of origin; only the lens branding is visible.
Photos show the lens looks generally clean, but there is no macro shot of the glass for fungus/haze/scratches or a test for autofocus.

risks.risk: Hidden fungus, haze, or internal dust not obvious from these angles; could affect image quality.
risks.proof: One clear macro photo of the front and rear glass under bright light (flashlight at an angle) plus a photo of the lens against a white background.
risks.if_unproven: Price as a lens that may have minor optical issues (assume not “like new”).

risks.risk: Scratches/chips on front or rear element edges (not fully visible).
risks.proof: Close-up of both elements’ edges (front and rear) with the lens tilted so the edge is in focus.
risks.if_unproven: Price as not guaranteed to be scratch-free.

risks.risk: Autofocus/AF-S motor may be weak or faulty (photos can’t confirm).
risks.proof: Short video of autofocus hunting and then locking on a nearby object (and a still photo showing focus).

risks.risk: Mount compatibility/condition (could be Nikon F mount but wear or bent contacts can exist).
risks.proof: Photo of the full rear mount contacts/contacts area in sharp focus.

proof_requests: Macro close-ups of front and rear glass (front + rear) with angled flashlight to reveal fungus/haze/scratches.
Sharp photo of the rear mount contacts/metal pins area.
Short autofocus test video (AF-S) showing it locks focus, plus a sample photo at 50mm.
response.reason: The lens model appears to be Nikon AF-S 50mm f/1.8G from the photos, but the key value drivers (optical condition and autofocus working status) are not provable from these images alone, so a safe worst-case price can’t be confidently selected from the comparables.
